one_line: A local-first registry and runtime that turns authenticated tabs into reviewed, bounded WebMCP action surfaces.
what_it_does: Packages reviewed site-specific actions, injects typed tools into the user's signed-in session, gates writes with human approval, and records receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: it creates typed, origin-bound, shared-state tools inside an existing authenticated tab, with drift failure and safety boundaries that pixel automation cannot match as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Demo frames show an action-pack registry/runtime and Last result/State output.
Description specifies exact origins, reviewed fingerprints, declarative manifests, bounded untrusted output, and human-gated writes.
Cross-service Grafana/Cal.com investigation is presented as the motivating workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent runtime concept and multiple staged action-pack states, but no live video and limited legibility cap end-to-end execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent registry, action-pack, execution, and result/state screens.
Devpost packaging aligns with the stated login/API, authorization, and receipts thesis.
impact_rationale: Operations teams working in authenticated systems without APIs have a concrete reliability and auditability problem; the proposed user-owned adoption path addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies monitoring, scheduling, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards as targets.
Human authorization and receipts address consequential operational actions.
creativity_rationale: Reframing the user's existing login as the API and distributing reviewed action packs is an original, ambitious adoption inversion for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: The registry/runtime plus reviewed-pack model is pursued across safety, origin binding, drift, and receipts.
Frames visibly present a packaged-action workflow rather than a single tool wrapper.
usability_note: The staged action-pack UI appears understandable, though dense and technical.
red_flags: No video submitted despite frame-sheet evidence; end-to-end runtime behavior is not directly observed.
Several metric labels and detailed states are not legible.
standouts: Strong safety model around authenticated sessions and consequential writes.
Clear WebMCP adoption thesis for sites that will never ship APIs.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with coherent visual evidence; live observation would resolve execution claims.

one_line: A deterministic URL-to-WebMCP manifest generator that profiles forms and waits for human approval.
what_it_does: Profiles a page, proposes read/write tools from detected forms, drafts webmcp.js with a digest, and verifies activation receipts.
leverage_rationale: Structured form-derived tools and digest/approval verification improve precision and repeatability over generic UI driving, but the same workflow remains possible with browser automation and the packet has no product frames.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies deterministic field tracing, JSON schemas, confirm gates for POST forms, SHA-256 manifest digests, and receipt verification.
Five named tools cover profile, proposal, drafting, approval staging, and verification.
execution_rationale: The stated flow is coherent and intentionally constrained, but there is no submitted video or gallery evidence to demonstrate the central URL-to-download workflow.
execution_evidence: About text describes a complete profile/propose/draft/approve/verify sequence.
Devpost screenshot is packaging only and does not show the live generator.
impact_rationale: Site owners and users need a low-friction way to expose forms to agents without hand-authoring integrations; deterministic generation addresses a real reliability problem.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets failed checkout/signup guesses and avoids requiring site-owner code.
Human approval is explicit before activation.
creativity_rationale: A no-model, deterministic compiler from real page forms to WebMCP tools is a fresh and disciplined angle on agent readiness.
creativity_evidence: No-language-model design and traceability from detected fields are distinctive choices.
Digest-backed receipts extend beyond simple form extraction.
usability_note: The one-link/one-approval flow is simple in concept; actual interface usability is unshown.
red_flags: No frame sheets, gallery images, or readable live workflow evidence submitted.
Claims of a working interface are primarily textual.
standouts: Deterministic, non-LLM generation with exact-text receipts.
Explicit inability of the activation tool to self-approve.
advance_reason: Promising concept but too little execution evidence for advancement in this claimed-execution stage.

one_line: A bounded Live Canvas where agents reshape storefronts, dashboards, or data tables to fit a user's intent.
what_it_does: Lets agents compose approved cards, badges, reports, and dashboard controls into a user-specific interface within constrained safe regions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP changes the product from a static UI into an agent-composable surface with shared live state; the bounded component toolbox makes composition more reliable than arbitrary browser manipulation.
leverage_evidence: Frames show a guided browser/content interface changing layouts and content in response to prompts.
Description names storefront curation, blank dashboard composition, and distributable datatable reports as WebMCP surfaces.
execution_rationale: The frame progression visibly supports a functioning adaptive-interface concept, though the exact agent calls and saved outputs are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show prompt/processing states and changed arrangements of content.
Devpost presentation and paint-led narrative consistently package BYOUI/Live Canvas.
impact_rationale: Adaptive interfaces can help shoppers research and help teams tailor dashboards, with credible value for users who need information organized around their current intent.
impact_evidence: Description identifies cart-abandonment/research friction and concrete storefront, CRM/ERP, and reporting use cases.
Frames show content being reorganized rather than merely described.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-interface and bounded agent composition is a genuinely memorable interaction model pursued across commerce, dashboards, and component distribution.
creativity_evidence: The product treats the interface itself as an agent-composed artifact.
Distinctive paint/creative framing and multiple scaling demos reinforce ambition.
usability_note: The prompt-led flow is approachable, but the breadth of modes may make the product harder to learn.
red_flags: Some detailed tool semantics and persistence behavior are not readable in frames.
standouts: Strong original concept of a bounded, agent-authored UI.
Safety-conscious constrained presets for untrusted public web content.
advance_reason: Distinctive concept with visible adaptive workflow and strong creative ambition.

one_line: A consent-first paperwork hub that turns one life-event sentence into reconciled, reviewable multi-portal forms.
what_it_does: Derives canonical facts, fills synthetic agency/insurer/employer forms, computes deadlines, flags conflicts, gates writes, and produces receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables page-scoped tools sharing the exact visible case state across independent portals, with dynamic registration and two-call human write gates; this is substantially more reliable than UI guessing.
leverage_evidence: Frames show intake, destination selection, populated forms, validation highlights, and approval modal.
Description specifies page-scoped registration/unregistration, canonical profile reconciliation, deadline math, and no-submit-before-click gates.
execution_rationale: The contact sheets visibly cover a coherent intake-to-populated-forms review flow with multiple states; final external filing is intentionally not performed and receipt detail is less visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show populated structured forms and review/confirmation states.
About text defines the complete bundle and explicitly keeps the human sovereign.
impact_rationale: Life-event paperwork across benefits, insurance, and employment is a high-friction, deadline-sensitive problem with a specific audience and direct demonstrated address.
impact_evidence: Description gives the concrete birth/dependent scenario and 30-day enrollment deadline.
Conflict reconciliation and one-time entry target repetitive, error-prone paperwork.
creativity_rationale: The multi-portal, canonical-fact and reconciliation model is an ambitious, memorable application of shared agent-human state to bureaucratic workflows.
creativity_evidence: Portal-scoped tool surfaces appear and disappear with page context.
Human-controlled normalization of conflicting names/dates is unusually thoughtful.
usability_note: The single-sentence intake and visible review gates are strong usability choices for a complex workflow.
red_flags: External portal submission and receipt contents are not clearly visible; demo uses synthetic portals.
standouts: Excellent end-to-end narrative from life event to reconciled forms.
Strong consent, reversibility, and conflict-explanation design.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly creative workflow with strong frame evidence and WebMCP-specific shared-state leverage.

one_line: An agent-native shopping site exposing discovery, cart, checkout, reviews, and orders as WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Combines a large product catalog with structured agent tools for searching, inspecting, comparing, cart management, user information, checkout, and order history.
leverage_rationale: Structured commerce operations can improve precision and multi-step repeatability over UI driving, but shopping outcomes remain broadly achievable by a general agent and the packet lacks live frame evidence.
leverage_evidence: About text claims a 123,133-product dataset and 15 tools spanning discovery through checkout/order history.
Devpost screenshot shows only a demo thumbnail with chat/action panels.
execution_rationale: The claimed scope is broad, but no frame sheets or direct live product evidence demonstrate catalog, cart, or checkout completion.
execution_evidence: Devpost packaging consistently presents CARTOS and an agent-native commerce thesis.
No readable storefront or transaction state is visible outside the embedded thumbnail.
impact_rationale: Shopping discovery and transaction assistance serve a clear audience, but the packet does not establish how much better this is than ordinary agent-assisted shopping.
impact_evidence: Description lists concrete shopping tasks and a real-world-sized catalog claim.
Tagline clearly targets humans and agents shopping together.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native ecommerce is a relevant synthesis with useful breadth, but the core concept is familiar and the evidence does not show a particularly novel interaction.
creativity_evidence: 15-tool commerce capability layer is broader than a recommendation chatbot.
Packaging emphasizes direct agent use of the site.
usability_note: The intended human/agent split is clear, but actual shopping usability is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or gallery workflow evidence.
Checkout and order completion claims are not visually verifiable in the packet.
standouts: Ambitious full-funnel commerce tool surface.
Large stated catalog gives the concept plausible breadth.
advance_reason: Potentially useful but execution and differentiation are insufficiently evidenced.

one_line: An accessible-by-default browser IDE where agents edit code, inspect previews, and run WCAG audits in one tab.
what_it_does: Provides multi-file editing, live preview, accessibility auditing, design-token checks, responsive preview, and browser compatibility tooling exposed through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to the same editor, preview, and audit state, closing the code-to-quality loop more reliably than separate UI automation handoffs.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly centers the shared editor/live-preview/WCAG loop.
Frame sheets show media only, so the WebMCP workflow itself is not visibly demonstrated.
execution_rationale: The packet contains a misleading/unrelated Rick Astley video and no actual editor/audit frames, so execution is thinly evidenced despite a coherent written scope.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot packages Blnq Studio and its stated capabilities.
Submitted frame sheets visibly depict the Rick Astley music video, not the claimed product.
impact_rationale: Front-end developers and teams have a real need for integrated accessibility checks, and catching violations during AI-assisted building directly addresses a common quality gap.
impact_evidence: About text identifies editor/audit handoff friction and WCAG violations as the target problem.
Named features include exact-element fixes and contrast checks.
creativity_rationale: Combining AI coding with same-tab accessibility auditing is a strong, focused interaction improvement, though the IDE category itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Design.md token enforcement and built-in baseline compatibility extend beyond a basic editor.
WebMCP is framed as the mechanism that closes the quality loop.
usability_note: A single-tab code/preview/audit workflow should reduce handoffs, but the actual UI is not shown.
red_flags: Video title and all frame sheets are Rick Astley music-video content unrelated to Blnq Studio.
No actual product interface or audit result is included.
standouts: Accessibility-first positioning is concrete and socially valuable.
Design-system and compatibility checks suggest thoughtful scope.
advance_reason: The submission media is unrelated, leaving the central product and agent workflow unverified.

one_line: A live flight-tail risk system that withdraws stale transport recommendations when aircraft evidence changes.
what_it_does: Evaluates organ-transport flight plans against cargo, aircraft-rotation, and delivery constraints, issues certificates, and dynamically invalidates tools when the plan becomes unsafe.
leverage_rationale: The defining behavior is WebMCP tool-surface mutation: selected/revalidate tools are unregistered when live evidence invalidates a plan, forcing the agent to replan rather than act on stale state.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly describes toolchange, unregistering get_selected_plan/revalidate_plan, and registering explain_invalidation/replan_mission.
Frames show risk dashboards, certificate-like outputs, and a visible -76 failure versus +33 viable margin.
execution_rationale: Video transcript and frame progression demonstrate a coherent operational scenario, quantified arithmetic, certificate output, aircraft swap, invalidation, and replanning.
execution_evidence: Transcript walks from UA417 -76 to UA623 +33, then aircraft swap to -11 and replan.
Frames show consistent dark operational UI, risk indicators, evidence panels, and results.
impact_rationale: Organ-transport coordinators face a specific, high-stakes problem where stale flight assumptions can cost a viable transplant; the product directly addresses safe operational reliance.
impact_evidence: Transcript specifies kidney time-on-ice, Chicago-to-Boston deadline, and cargo/rotation/delivery constraints.
The system names the binding constraint and removes unsafe recommendations.
creativity_rationale: Treating changing tool availability as a machine-readable invalidation signal for a live-world recommendation is exceptionally original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: The project centers on semantic tool withdrawal rather than errors or disabled buttons.
Certificate fingerprints, validity horizon, tail number, and explicit replan path form a memorable interaction model.
usability_note: The page names binding constraints and recommendation status clearly, though the domain is necessarily specialized.
red_flags: Demo is a simulation/prototype rather than a live carrier integration, but this does not negate the demonstrated concept.
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP-specific invalidation semantics.
High-stakes use case with transparent arithmetic and certificates.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage, impact, creativity, and unusually complete video evidence.

one_line: A consent-first benefit navigator with shared visible state, reversible staging, and review-packet preparation.
what_it_does: Searches a synthetic benefits directory, inspects requirements, assesses case readiness, manages consent, stages up to three plans, and prepares a local packet without submitting applications.
leverage_rationale: Narrow tools tied to the exact visible case state improve structured assistance and auditability, but the packet shows a conceptual diagram only and the same basic research workflow is possible with UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Devpost screenshot diagrams read tools, visible workspace, and write tools.
About text specifies seven narrow tools, immediate visible changes, reversibility, and submitted:false.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and safety-conscious, but only a static architecture/presentation diagram is visible; no live case workflow or packet output is demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Screenshot clearly names read/workspace/write stages and reset capability.
Description defines a synthetic directory and demo case but provides no observed interaction.
impact_rationale: Benefit navigation is a real, consequential paperwork problem, and visible/reversible preparation can help people while preserving decision authority; the synthetic-only scope limits evidence of practical reach.
impact_evidence: Description identifies eligibility evidence, consent, readiness gaps, and application planning.
The final tool explicitly never submits or sends evidence.
creativity_rationale: The consent-first shared-workspace boundary is a thoughtful synthesis of agent assistance and benefit paperwork, though the interaction is not shown beyond the diagram.
creativity_evidence: Explicit visible, reversible state and activity log are central rather than decorative.
Reset and consent tools encode the safety model.
usability_note: Visible/reversible planning should be approachable, but no actual user flow is shown.
red_flags: No video, frame sheets, or live interaction evidence.
Synthetic directory and non-submitting scope leave real-world completion untested.
standouts: Clear human-sovereignty and reversibility boundary.
Good separation of read tools, shared state, and write tools.
advance_reason: Well-specified safety concept, but execution and agent behavior are not demonstrated.

one_line: A real-time wildfire simulation and decision-support map with structured recommendations and human-approved plans.
what_it_does: Visualizes fire spread, weather, threatened areas, and units; runs and compares simulations; stages tactical plans; and gates commit/revert actions behind human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured simulation inspection, comparison, and staged commit/revert are a meaningful improvement over an agent clicking a complex map, though a general agent could approximate much of the UI workflow.
leverage_evidence: Frames show an evolving map with fire overlays, markers, side panels, and operational controls.
Description claims 21 structured tools covering inspect, simulate, compare, prepare, commit, and revert.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence visibly demonstrates a stateful wildfire simulation with changing overlays and controls, while exact agent invocation and final approval are less legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show map progression, expanding/changing fire regions, markers, and panels.
About text describes a staged-plan workflow with reversible actions.
impact_rationale: Incident commanders and response teams have a real high-stakes need to visualize evolving fire conditions and compare tactics; the human approval boundary is appropriate.
impact_evidence: Description names resources, weather, evacuation, threatened areas, and tactical planning.
Interactive map visibly represents operational scenario evolution.
creativity_rationale: AI-assisted wildfire simulation with staged human approval is an ambitious and valuable synthesis, though simulation/decision-support is an established category.
creativity_evidence: 21-tool surface and commit/revert plan model pursue a complete operational loop.
Real-time map evolution is visibly integrated with recommendations.
usability_note: Map-plus-panel layout communicates a complex scenario, though emergency operations interfaces are inherently dense.
red_flags: Exact tool calls and human approval completion are not fully legible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Strong domain fit for structured state and simulation comparison.
Reversible staged plans preserve operator authority.
advance_reason: Credible interactive simulation evidence and a strong, high-impact decision-support use case.

one_line: A 2D/3D apartment planner where people edit spaces visually and agents manipulate semantic geometry and furnishings.
what_it_does: Creates apartment projects, edits walls/openings/finishes, places dimensioned furniture, checks fit, renders 3D/sunlight previews, and exposes scene/history tools to agents.
leverage_rationale: Semantic scene tools let an agent inspect and modify geometry, furniture, finishes, and history precisely without dragging pixels; shared 2D/3D state makes this materially better than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Frames show evolving floor plans, apartment editor panels, and product/furniture pages.
Description specifies a meter-based scene document shared by editor, saved data, fit checks, and renderer, plus page-scoped tools.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets visibly cover presenter demo, layout editing, and furnishing/product discovery with a coherent apartment-planning workflow; exact tool invocation is not fully readable.
execution_evidence: Frames show floor plan evolving from simple to more complex geometry.
Frames also show furniture-related product listings and the Devpost preview pairing agent/chat with design workspace.
impact_rationale: Apartment hunters and planners have a concrete need to test furniture fit, circulation, and livability before committing; the product directly supports those decisions.
impact_evidence: Description names bed/table fit, circulation, rooms, and 2D/3D inspection.
Furniture dimensions and fit checks address practical planning uncertainty.
creativity_rationale: Combining semantic architectural editing, agent collaboration, 3D visualization, and real-world furnishing discovery is an ambitious, memorable workflow.
creativity_evidence: One scene document drives multiple representations and fit checks.
Agent tools cover geometry and presentation settings rather than only text search.
usability_note: Visual editing plus conversational assistance is promising, but the tool is complex and requires login/project setup.
red_flags: Login requirement adds friction; exact WebMCP calls are not clearly visible in contact sheets.
Some product listing details are too small to verify.
standouts: Strong shared semantic scene model across 2D, 3D, and agent tools.
Practical bridge from apartment geometry to furniture selection.
advance_reason: Well-demonstrated, high-value planning workflow where structured agent manipulation is materially useful.
